<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Bhuvanābyudaya is an epic poem written in Sanskrit by Śaṅkuka in the 9th century AD. The poem is divided into four parts that explore different aspects of the universe. The first part describes the creation of the universe, including the emergence of Brahma, the creator, and the creation of the earth, the sun, the moon, and the stars. The second part describes the geography of the earth, including the continents and the oceans, as well as various mythical places. The third part describes the exploits of various gods and goddesses, including Śiva and Pārvatī, Viṣṇu and his avatāra-s, and Durgā and her battles against demons. The fourth and final part, known as the Vikramāditya Carita, tells the story of the hero Vikramāditya and his adventures and battles with gods and demons. Bhuvanābyudaya is known for its rich descriptions of the natural world and its complex poetic structures, and it is considered one of the most significant works of Sanskrit literature.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Bhuvanābyudaya is a poem that is divided into four parts that explore different aspects of the universe. The contents of each part are:<br><br>Part 1 - Sarga Khaṇḍa<br><br>Describes the creation of the universe and the emergence of Brahma, the creator, from the navel of Viṣṇu.<br>Describes the creation of the earth, the sun, the moon, and the stars, as well as the various creatures that inhabit the universe.<br>Explores the concepts of time, karma, and rebirth.<br><br>Part 2 - Pṛthivī Khaṇḍa<br><br>Describes the geography of the earth, including the seven continents and the seven oceans.<br>Describes various mythical places, such as the city of the gods, the land of the demons, and the land of the Nāgas.<br>Explores the natural world, including rivers, mountains, forests, and animals.<br><br>Part 3 - Deva Khaṇḍa<br><br>Describes the exploits of various gods and goddesses, including Śiva and Pārvatī, Viṣṇu and his avatāra-s, and Durgā and her battles against demons.<br>Explores the nature of devotion and the relationship between gods and humans.<br><br>Part 4 - Vikramāditya Khaṇḍa (also known as Vikramāditya Carita)<br><br>Tells the story of King Vikramāditya and his adventures and battles with gods and demons.<br>Explores the nature of dharma, or righteous duty, and the importance of justice and morality in ruling a kingdom.<br>The story includes battles with supernatural beings, such as the demon king Vātāpi and the sorcerer Bhaṭṭi, as well as encounters with gods and goddesses, including Śiva and Pārvatī.<br>This part is also known as the Vikramāditya Carita and is considered a separate work by some scholars.</div></div></div>

<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Bhuvanābyudaya by Śaṅkuka is a significant contribution to Sanskrit literature. The epic poem explores the creation of the universe, the geography of the earth, the exploits of various gods and goddesses, and the adventures of King Vikramāditya. The poem is known for its rich descriptions of the natural world, its complex poetic structures, and its influence on later Indian literature and culture. Bhuvanābyudaya has had a lasting impact on Indian art, music, and philosophy, and it is considered one of the most important works of Sanskrit literature, serving as a source of inspiration for generations of poets and writers.</div></div></div>
